Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires and the India Women players are back out in the middle. Ainna Hashim and Winifred Duraisingam are the openers for Malaysia Women. Pooja Vastrakar has the new ball in hand.
... The Run Chase ...

Malaysia Women's bowling showed signs of inexperience as they delivered a slew of full tosses, offering the Indian batters ample opportunities to unleash their strokes. Furthermore, misfields and three dropped catches proved to be costly for the Malaysians. Now, Malaysia faces the daunting task of chasing down a massive target of 174 in 90 balls on a wicket conducive to batting. However, they will have to contend with India's experienced bowling attack. The stage is set for an intriguing second innings, and cricket fans can't afford to miss it. Stay tuned as we witness whether Malaysia can pull off a remarkable chase or if India's bowlers can maintain their dominance.

India's batting got off to a flying start with captain Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma setting the tone. While Mandhana departed after a quickfire 27 off 16 balls, Shafali Verma held the fort and played a spectacular innings, scoring 67 off just 39 deliveries, featuring 4 boundaries and 5 towering sixes. Jemimah Rodrigues also joined the party, notching up 47 runs off 29 balls at number 3, sharing an explosive 87-run partnership with Shafali. Late in the innings, Richa Ghosh added fireworks with a cameo of 21 runs off a mere 7 balls. The top four Indian batters took charge, propelling their team to an imposing total.

The first innings of Quarter Final 1 of the Asian Games Women's Cricket competition has concluded with India Women posting a formidable total of 173/2 in just 15 overs, after some rain-induced drama that shortened the game. India has set a challenging target of 174 runs in 90 balls for Malaysia Women to chase down.

Just a single to end but 20 runs come off the final over and India Women finish with a mammoth total on the board. This is banged in a bit short around off, Jemimah Rodrigues rocks back and pulls it straight to deep mid-wicket for one, ending unbeaten on 47. India Women finish with 173/2 in their 15 overs!

Malaysia Women come into this contest as the underdogs but do have a few players who can inflict pain to the opposition. They have already played a match against Hong Kong Women and won that game quite convincingly which will certainly boost their confidence. Can Malaysia Women notch up probably their biggest victory ever? Or will India Women cruise to victory? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

India Women are a force to reckon with in world cricket at the moment but their last tour up in Bangladesh wasn't one of their best. The batters struggled to score runs and at times, they were out-bowled by the opposition spinners. This, however, is a great way to get back in the groove and stamp their authority in the Asian Games, at which they will be making their debut at the Women's cricket competition.

Hello and welcome to Quarterfinal 1 of the Asian Games Women's cricket competition where India Women will go up against Malaysia Women. The sport returns to the Asian Games for the first time since 2014 and India Women will be one of the favorites to get the Gold medal. Can Malaysia Women spring a surprise here?
... MATCH DAY ...

After a year-long delay due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Asian Games are finally here, and this sporting spectacle promises to be bigger and better than ever before. This 19th edition of the Asiad, taking place in Hangzhou, China, is even more special for cricket fans with the reintroduction of the sport. Cricket has returned to the Asian Games in the T20 format for the first time since 2014, with both men's and women's teams in their respective disciplines competing for medals. The preliminary round of the women's competition is done and dusted, and it is now time for Quarter-Final 1 between India Women and Malaysia Women at the ZJUT Cricket Field in Hangzhou. India Women, in their cricketing debut at the Asian Games campaign, are one of the favourites to bag the gold medal. Harmanpreet Kaur -led India are coming off an ordinary tour of Bangladesh, where they did manage to clinch the T20I series but faltered in the ODI series. In what can be seen as a knee-jerk reaction, the Women I'm Blue have made changes to their squad for this all-important competition. The promising Yastika Bhatia has been left out, and with Richa Ghosh's return, she is likely to don the gloves for India. Harmanpreet Kaur is currently serving a two-match ban for breaching the ICC's code of conduct during the ODI series in Bangladesh and will be available for the final should India Women reach there. In her absence, the Women in Blue will heavily rely on the trio of Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, and Jemimah Rodrigues. Deepti Sharma, Devika Vaidya, and Amanjot Kaur retain their places in the all-rounders' group, which sees the addition of uncapped Kanika Ahuja. They were dealt a late blow in their preparations for the Asian Games, with left-arm pacer Anjali Sarvani ruled out due to a knee injury. Pooja Vastrakar has been named as her replacement and is likely to form a pair with the Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup star, Titas Sadhu, who has received her maiden call-up to the senior team. In the spin department, Rajeshwari Gayakwad will hold the key, with Minnu Mani as the other spin bowling option. On the other hand, Malaysia Women are coming off a comprehensive victory over Hong Kong in their opening encounter of the Asian Games. After being put into bat, contributions from Winifred Duraisingam, Wan Julia, and Mahirah Izzati Ismail helped them post 104 on the board. With the ball, they kept picking wickets at regular intervals and were even helped by some indecisive running by the Hong Kong batters. As they prepare to get over India in this knockout fixture, skipper Winifred Duraisingam will have to lead from the front with the bat. Mas Elysa did not have the best of outings against Hong Kong, and she will be eager to take her game up a notch. In the past year, Mahirah Izzati Ismail has been instrumental in contributing with both bat and ball, and a lot will depend on her if Malaysia Women are to pose a stiff threat to India Women. Other than the off-spinner Mahirah, the onus with the ball will also be on the pace duo of Ainna Hashim and Aisya Eleesa. In the previous two meetings between these two sides, India got the better of Malaysia on both occasions by a convincing margin. Will India Women extend their dominance? Or will the third time be the charm for Malaysia Women? We will find out together.
